name: Oculocutaneous Albinism

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in sub-Saharan African populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Oculocutaneous Albinism

criteria.description: Congenital hypopigmentation of skin and hair
Hypopigmentation of the iris and retina with associated visual abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic variants in OCA-related genes (e.g., TYR, OCA2, TYRP1, SLC45A2)
Evidence of foveal hypoplasia on ophthalmologic examination or imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital hypopigmentation of skin/hair and ocular hypopigmentation with visual abnormalities; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for definitive diagnosis and subtype classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital generalized hypopigmentation of skin and hair
searchTerms: born with pale skin and hair
general lack of pigmentation from birth

occasional.symptomName: Prone to sunburn and skin damage
searchTerms: susceptible to sunburn and skin injury

rare.symptomName: Skin malignancies (e.g., basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma)
searchTerms: skin cancers like basal or squamous cell

rare.notes: Rarely associated, more common in syndromic albinism

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying pathogenic variants in TYR, OCA2, TYRP1, SLC45A2 genes
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing foveal hypoplasia
genetic: Mutations in melanin biosynthesis pathway genes
other: Visual evoked potentials showing misrouting of optic nerve fibers
Skin biopsy demonstrating reduced or absent melanin pigment

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily ocular involvement with minimal or no skin hypopigmentation
Albinism with immunodeficiency and bleeding tendency
Presence of giant lysosomal granules in leukocytes
Distinct facial features such as dystopia canthorum

redFlags: Rapid onset of skin lesions or suspicious pigmented lesions
Recurrent infections or bleeding suggestive of syndromic albinism
references: Grønskov K, Ek J, Brondum-Nielsen K. Oculocutaneous albinism. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:43.
Kruijt CC, et al. Clinical and molecular aspects of oculocutaneous albinism. Pigment Cell Melanoma Res. 2018;31(3): 325-338.
Oetting WS, King RA. Molecular basis of albinism: mutations and polymorphisms of pigmentation genes associated with albinism. Hum Mutat. 1999;13(2):99-115.
